notes.title: [PLACEHOLDER] Complex contagion
notes.science: [PLACEHOLDER] Some things spread only when several neighbors do them first, not just one.
notes.limits: [PLACEHOLDER] Each starling here counts only its seven nearest birds.
notes.counter: [PLACEHOLDER] Some ideas spread from one friend alone.
notes.question: [PLACEHOLDER] What would you do only once enough friends did it?

notes.title: [PLACEHOLDER] The majority illusion
notes.science: [PLACEHOLDER] When the best-known birds fly, it can look as if most birds fly.
notes.limits: [PLACEHOLDER] The water's picture here is one simple weighting.
notes.counter: [PLACEHOLDER] Often what looks common really is common.
notes.question: [PLACEHOLDER] Who do you see most, and are they like everyone else?
